subject: Private deployment: licensing boundary, evidence delivery and proposed timeline
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medsyshealth.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medsyshealth.com
Date: 2026-12-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment questions: license scope + evidence timeline

Hi Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we're drafting the purchase paperwork, Legal and our Security team have a couple of specific asks about the Private (VPC) deployment option that I'd like to clarify before we exchange final redlines:

1) License scope: we need explicit language that the license is limited to the provisioned dedicated instances for Medsys (no broader distribution or sublicensing). Can you confirm how Redwood proposes to word that in the Order Form or an MSA appendix?

2) Evidence & audit timeline: our auditors want a clear timeline for delivery of the evidence package (snapshots, KV cache proof of access, audit logs) and a list of what you'll provide vs what we need to self-collect.

3) Operator access during audit window: we may request temporary console access for a 48-hour supervised test. What gating controls / attestation can Redwood provide?

I've attached the current Order Form draft for reference. Can someone on your side propose a short timeline and a one-page list of deliverables?

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Head of IT Risk — Medsys Health
Attachments: OrderForm_Draft_Medsys.docx

From: connor.obrien@redwood.com
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-09T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: license scope + evidence timeline

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick ack — we'll scope this as follows and then Laura can propose contract language:

- License boundary: Redwood proposes an MSA Appendix A (Private Deployment) that states "License limited to Customer-provisioned dedicated instances / environments specified in the Order Form; no rights to redistribute or sublicense." We can add a short definition of "dedicated instance" tied to the Order Form ID.

- Evidence inventory: we'll provide the following deliverables within the schedule below:
  * Access attestation (KMS custody statement)
  * Snapshot manifest (hash + timestamp) of the deployed model binary and environment
  * Audit log extract (rolling 90 days; redacted tokens)
  * Operator activity summary for any supervised access windows

- Proposed delivery timeline (draft):
  * T0 = contract signature
  * T0+10 business days: evidence inventory spreadsheet + KMS attestation
  * T0+25 business days: full snapshot manifest + audit log extract (sample window)

On operator access: we can enable a restricted, time-limited support session with session recording and a signed attestation of activity. We'd like to agree on a scope doc for what testers may and may not do during that 48-hour window.

Laura — can you weigh in with specific redline language and any legal caveats we should expect?

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-10T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: license scope + evidence timeline

Connor / team —

Thanks, Connor — I've reviewed Sarah's asks and sketched redline language and constraints below. High level: Medsys' requests are reasonable but we need to be explicit about operator limitation and data-handling carveouts.

Suggested MSA appendix language (excerpt):
"Appendix A — Private Deployment License. Subject to the Order Form, Redwood grants Customer a non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to use Redwood's software and model artifacts solely within the Customer-provisioned dedicated instances identified in the Order Form. Customer may not copy, redistribute, or make available the software or model artifacts outside the scope of the dedicated instances without prior written consent."
Operator access clause (excerpt):
"Redwood may provide temporary, auditable operator access for the purpose of supporting Customer audits or for supervised testing. Such access will be: (i) limited in duration and scope as agreed in a mutually executed access scope document; (ii) session-recorded and logged; and (iii) subject to a required operator attestation signed by Redwood's authorized engineer. Redwood shall not be required to provide unfettered console access or keys enabling Customer to exfiltrate model weights."
Evidence delivery and limitations:
"Redwood will provide a manifest of deployed artifacts, cryptographic hashes, and an extract of operational audit logs as described in the Order Form. Sensitive customer data and raw token-level content will be redacted in compliance with Redwood's privacy policy. Redwood's obligation is limited to delivering the artifacts described; any additional forensics or live replication services may be subject to a professional services fee."
Timing: the schedule Connor proposed looks fine; propose adding a 5-business day review buffer after each delivery milestone for Medsys' auditors to ask clarifying questions.

Risks / legal caveats: 
- We cannot hand over private keys or unencrypted model weights.
- If Medsys requests a longer retention or specific infrastructure snapshots (e.g., full disk images), we should route to Professional Services for scope + cost.

I'll prepare a redline PDF (MSA_v3_Redlines.pdf) with the above sections and send back.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_v3_Redlines.pdf

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medsyshealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medsyshealth.com
Date: 2026-12-11T10:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: license scope + evidence timeline

Hi Laura / Connor —

Appreciate the quick review. A few clarifications from our side:

- License: the proposed Appendix A language is OK, but Security wants explicit confirmation that the license is limited to "model inference and runtime execution" and excludes any rights to persist or export the model binaries for external use. Can you add that phrase?

- Evidence: we need the manifest and hashes plus a short proof-of-rotation note for KMS keys (who holds the root, how is rotation logged). If Redwood can't provide root-level attestations, please confirm what the attestation will state (e.g., "Redwood holds and rotates the operational keys used to encrypt model artifacts and can confirm rotation events for the period requested").

- Operator access: our auditors want a pre-specified test script for the 48-hour window (steps, expected outputs, redline items). Would Redwood accept a joint-runbook sign-off 5 business days before the window?

Proposed phased schedule:
  * Signature + Order Form sign-off: 2026-12-13
  * T0+7bd: evidence inventory CSV (we attached the template) + KMS attestation
  * T0+20bd: snapshot manifest and audit log extract (sample)
  * T0+30bd: supervised 48-hour access window (optional)

If you can confirm the KMS attestation wording and the runbook sign-off timeline, we can circulate the Order Form back to procurement for internal approvals.

Thanks,
Sarah

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.lin@medsyshealth.com
Date: 2026-12-12T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: license scope + evidence timeline

Looping in from Sales Ops perspective —

Medsys' ask for a runbook sign-off and a KMS attestation during the audit window is reasonable but represents a small SLA carveout. Options to consider:

1) Offer the attestation and runbook sign-off (no charge) but limit to one audit window per 12 months; OR
2) Provide extended evidence or additional snapshot support as a billable Professional Services engagement.

If Legal (Laura) can accept the Appendix A + attestation language Connor suggested (with Sarah's "inference and runtime execution" phrase added), I recommend we approve option 1 to keep the deal momentum. We should also prepare a short addendum for the Order Form noting the one-time supervised access window and the approval flow (PS to roll in if more than one window requested).

Happy to approve if Legal signs off on the exact wording and the procurement folks accept the one-window limit.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Sales

Sarah / Procurement —

Thanks everyone for the quick input. Attached is a consolidated plan: MSA_v3_Redlines.pdf (legal redlines), OrderForm_Draft_Medsys.docx (updated to include Appendix A reference), and the evidence-inventory-template.csv filled in with the deliverables we propose to provide.

Key commitments we can make now:
- Appendix A will include the phrase "model inference and runtime execution" to clarify license boundary.
- KMS attestation will state Redwood holds and rotates operational keys and can confirm rotation events for the requested period; Redwood will not hand over root private keys.
- Evidence delivery timeline (post-signature): T0+7bd inventory and attestation; T0+20bd snapshot manifest + logs; T0+30bd supervised 48-hour window (subject to runbook sign-off 5bd prior).
- One supervised access window included at no charge; subsequent windows go to PS.

Next steps: 
1) Sarah/procurement to confirm they can sign by 2026-12-16 to hit the proposed schedule.
2) Laura to circulate the redline PDF to Sarah for comment (attached).
3) Connor to open a HubSpot task (004892-Medsys) and share the DocuSign link once procurement confirms.

DocuSign & HubSpot links will follow in a separate email.
